device.name: LED desk lamp
device.subtitle: Light · balance · current
device.configurationNote: Generic LED desk lamp with an articulated arm; no particular manufacturer's construction is implied.

components.title: LED module
components.role: Turns electrical energy into light directed at your desk.
components.mechanism: Current produces light in a semiconductor; a phosphor can convert some of that light to create a white blend.
components.assembly: This illustration places the LED board beneath a shade, with a metal thermal path carrying heat away.

preview.mechanism: A semiconductor emits light; phosphor helps make it white.
preview.assembly: LED board, optical cover and a path for heat to escape.

components.title: LED driver
components.role: Controls the electrical current supplied to the LED module.
components.mechanism: A current regulator adjusts its output to maintain the intended LED current, while dimming changes that target or pulses the light.
components.assembly: The illustrated driver board connects the power input, brightness control and LED module; real lamps may put it in an external adapter.

preview.role: Supplies controlled current to the LEDs.
preview.mechanism: Adjusting current or pulse timing changes brightness.
preview.assembly: Power input → driver board → LED module.

components.title: Articulated arm
components.role: Positions the light without moving the whole lamp.
components.mechanism: Gravity turns the arm around its pivots; joint friction or a balancing spring must oppose that turning effect to hold the head still.
components.assembly: Linked arm sections meet at pivots, with the head at one end and the base supporting the other.

preview.role: Moves the light to your workspace.
preview.mechanism: Joint resistance counters gravity's turning effect.

components.title: Weighted base
components.role: Supports the arm and helps the lamp resist tipping.
components.mechanism: A broad, heavy base helps keep the combined center of mass above the support area as the head moves outward.
components.assembly: The illustrated base holds a dense weight beneath a cover and connects to the arm's lower pivot.

preview.mechanism: The combined center of mass stays over the footprint.
preview.assembly: Weight, outer cover and arm mount.

concepts.title: LED light
concepts.summary: The lamp and your laptop both use LEDs to produce light.
concepts.explanation: An LED produces light when current flows through its semiconductor. A white-light design can use phosphor to convert part of a blue LED's output. A lamp lights your desk; the MacBook's mini-LED backlight illuminates LCD pixels.
concepts.tryThis: Compare the lamp's LED module with the MacBook display.
concepts.scopeNote: Shared principle; LED size, optics and control differ between the objects.

concepts.title: Current control
concepts.summary: Control current to control an LED's output.
concepts.explanation: An LED's current can change steeply with a small voltage change. A driver regulates current instead of simply applying a fixed voltage. Brightness can be varied by changing current or switching it rapidly on and off.
concepts.tryThis: Change brightness and watch the light output respond.

concepts.title: Balance & torque
concepts.summary: Moving the head changes the turning effect of its weight.
concepts.explanation: The farther a load extends horizontally from a pivot, the more torque its weight produces. The arm must resist that torque, and the whole lamp stays upright while its combined center of mass remains over the base's support area.
concepts.tryThis: Compare the lamp's reach with the width of its base.

device.name: Cordless drill
device.subtitle: Motion · torque · energy
device.configurationNote: Generic brushless cordless drill with a lithium-ion pack; no particular manufacturer's layout, voltage or performance is implied.

components.title: Brushless motor
components.role: Converts electrical power into rotation for the gearbox.
components.mechanism: Electronics energize coils in sequence, creating magnetic forces that keep a permanent-magnet rotor turning.
components.assembly: The conceptual motor contains stationary copper coils around a magnetic rotor supported by a shaft and bearings.

preview.mechanism: Sequenced coil currents keep a magnetic rotor turning.
preview.assembly: Coils around a rotor, shaft and bearings.

components.title: Reduction gears
components.role: Reduces motor speed and increases the torque available at the chuck.
components.mechanism: Meshing gears trade rotational speed for turning force; friction means the output receives less power than the motor supplies.
components.assembly: The illustrated gear module sits between the motor shaft and chuck; its shapes explain reduction without reproducing a particular drill's gear train.

preview.mechanism: Gear ratio sets the speed reduction and ideal torque gain.
preview.assembly: A compact gear train links motor and chuck.

components.title: Three-jaw chuck
components.role: Centers and grips a drill bit so it turns with the output shaft.
components.mechanism: Three jaws move inward together; their clamping force creates friction that resists a round bit slipping.
components.assembly: A rotating sleeve surrounds three guided jaws connected to the drill's output shaft.

preview.mechanism: Three jaws clamp the shank and resist slip.
preview.assembly: Sleeve, guided jaws and output shaft.

components.title: Battery pack
components.role: Stores the energy that powers the drill away from a socket.
components.mechanism: Chemical reactions drive electrons around the external circuit while ions move inside the cells, supplying power to the motor controller.
components.assembly: The conceptual pack groups cells, electrical contacts and control electronics inside a protective enclosure.

preview.mechanism: Chemical reactions drive current through the motor circuit.
preview.assembly: Cells and contacts within a protective pack.

concepts.title: Electric motors
concepts.summary: Current in coils creates the magnetic forces that turn a rotor.
concepts.explanation: A brushless motor switches current between coils in sequence. Their magnetic fields act on the rotor's permanent magnets to sustain rotation. The same broad conversion from electricity to motion also powers the laptop's cooling fans.
concepts.scopeNote: Shared motor principle; no claim that the drill and laptop use identical motor designs.

concepts.title: Gear reduction
concepts.summary: Lower output speed can provide more output torque.
concepts.explanation: In an ideal 4:1 reduction, four input turns produce one output turn and four times the input torque. Real gears lose some power to friction and have strength limits. The ratio trades speed for torque; it does not create energy.
concepts.tryThis: Compare the fast motor shaft with the slower chuck.
concepts.scopeNote: The 4:1 ratio is an illustrative example, not this model's specification.

concepts.title: Grip & friction
concepts.summary: Friction lets the chuck transmit torque to a round bit.
concepts.explanation: The chuck presses its jaws against the bit. Static friction opposes relative slipping, letting the bit turn with the chuck up to the available grip. In the gearbox, unwanted friction instead dissipates some energy as heat.
concepts.tryThis: Trace torque from the gears through the jaws to the bit.
